subject: Week 20: participatory music class window opens - enroll one
bodyText:
This week
Days 138-144 approach the 6-month landmark: sitting with progressively less support, deliberate object examination (turn, mouth, transfer), and reduplicated babble (baba, dada - non-referential at this stage). Rolling is fluid for some; the CDC tummy-to-back checkpoint remains 6 months. His iron stores are beginning their pre-6-month depletion - solids will backfill via fortified cereal and iron-rich foods.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Mini sleep disruptions at developmental leaps even with the 4-month regression behind you - hold the routine steady rather than re-engineering it.
- [low concern] Dada with no referent - reduplicated babble is a language milestone, not a first word; referential use comes months later.
- [monitor] Persistent failure to roll, sit with support, or transfer objects hand to hand - flag for the 6-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Acute illness onset or persistent feeding difficulties - same-day call.
- [call now] Fever of 102F rectal or higher with lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips - 911 for breathing or color change.

Enrichment opportunities
- Enroll one weekly participatory music class. The Gerry/Unrau/Trainor 2012 randomized trial found active classes at 6 months beat passive listening on pitch and rhythm discrimination and prelinguistic gestures. Music Together SF runs rolling 10-week babies sessions ($405, or $380 on auto-enroll; enroll about two weeks before a session start); SFCM Smart Start's fixed August registration has passed for this fall, so Music Together is the live option. One class is the right dose - no dose-response evidence exists under 12 months. Gerry, Unrau & Trainor 2012 (PubMed): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Start Suzuki listening if early instrumental training is the plan: settle the instrument (violin and piano are the common calls), order the Book 1-2 repertoire recordings, and run them 30+ minutes a day during play or feeds. Years of listening precede lessons at age 3-4; the cost of the option now is recordings only. Suzuki Association of the Americas: https://suzukiassociation.org/
- Rotate in hand-eye coordination toys: stacking rings (target the ring toward the post) and a shape-sorter used for open exploration - sorting itself is not the goal yet.
- Shift read-alouds toward dialogue: ask what's-that and pause for a response even though he is pre-verbal - the turn-taking, not the answer, is the input. AAP - Early Literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/

Upcoming
- Day 168-182 (Oct 26-Nov 9, 2026): 6-month well visit - book now if it is not on the calendar; the iron/hemoglobin screen and solids-readiness assessment happen here.
- Oct 2026-Mar 2027: RSV season - put RSV questions on the 6-month visit list, and review circulating-illness patterns if he is in group care.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses voice to express joy and displeasure
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Distinct vocalizations for different states — early affective communication.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-voice-for-joy/complete

- Rolls from back to tummy
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Harder direction; requires more core and upper-body strength.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/rolls-back-to-tummy/complete

- Reaches for objects with one hand
  AAP window: day 120-210
  What to look for: Differentiation from earlier two-handed swiping — emerging hand preference is normal but unstable until ~age 3.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/reaches-with-one-hand/complete

- Pushes up with straight arms during tummy time
  AAP window: day 120-180
  What to look for: Full arm extension, chest off the floor. Builds toward sitting.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/leans-on-hands-tummy-time/complete

- Leans on hands to support self when sitting
  AAP window: day 120-180
  What to look for: Tripod sit. Precedes hands-free sitting by 1-2 months.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/sits-with-hand-support/complete
